target.title: fix(sms): isolate validated webhook quotas per sender
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The SMS webhook's accepted-callback quota was keyed by resolved client address. Twilio shares egress addresses across unrelated senders, so one flooding sender could exhaust the 30/minute callback budget and make valid callbacks from other users fail with HTTP 429.

## Why This Change Was Made

The patch keeps the existing pre-validation failed-request budget keyed by account, route, and client address, then uses two post-validation limits: sender fairness plus bounded account/route admission.

- Signature-validated callbacks use `resolveTwilioInboundSender(form)`, so equivalent SMS and `RCS:` address forms share one sender bucket.
- A true single-sender overload remains observable as HTTP 429; the handler does not acknowledge and silently discard it.
- Another validated sender behind the same Twilio egress address remains dispatchable.
- All validated senders on an account/route share a 300/minute aggregate ceiling, so high-cardinality signed fan-out cannot create unbounded durable-ingress pressure.
- With `dangerouslyDisableSignatureValidation`, `From` is unauthenticated, so the stricter callback budget stays keyed to the resolved client address and cannot be bypassed by rotating sender text.

## User Impact

One abusive or bursty sender can no longer cross-throttle unrelated SMS users behind Twilio's shared infrastructure. The existing 30/minute sender threshold and invalid-request behavior remain unchanged, while the new 300/minute account/route ceiling keeps aggregate overload fail-closed and visible.

The 10:1 aggregate-to-sender ratio permits multiple active senders without recreating the shared-egress bug, while preserving an explicit absolute ceiling for durable ingress.

## Evidence

Current contributor head: `bdd8173fd6a` on upstream `main` `aad27e26296`.

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/sms/src/webhook.test.ts`: 13/13 passed, including the sender-isolation and aggregate fan-out regressions.
- Positive regression: 30 callbacks from sender A are accepted; sender B on the same egress address is still accepted.
- Negative regression: sender A's 31st callback returns 429 even when its address changes from SMS E.164 syntax to equivalent `RCS:+1 (555) 123-4567` syntax and even when the egress IP changes.
- Signature-disabled regression: rotating `From` values does not widen the address-keyed quota.
- Invalid/missing canonical senders share an empty-sender bucket without consuming a valid sender's quota.
- High-cardinality regression: 300 distinct signed senders are accepted on one account/route and the 301st returns 429 without enqueueing.
- Fixed-window recovery regression: the sender becomes dispatchable after the window expires.
- Direct formatter check and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- The pre-PR plan gate passed for extension, extension-test, and docs lanes with no dependency-sensitive changes.

### Real behavior proof

The focused suite drives the real request-body parser, Twilio HMAC validation, canonical sender resolver, fixed-window limiter, response writer, and durable-ingress seam with realistic HTTP requests. It proves both the intended isolation and the closest bypasses without deploying the Gateway.

No live Twilio callback was sent to this exact branch head, and no Gateway restart or production webhook change was performed. A maintainer-controlled live Twilio smoke remains the strongest optional transport proof.

AI-assisted; reviewed and validated before submission.
